2167.t: Etymology tree Biblical Hebrew מִרְיָם (miryɔm)bor. Aramaic מריםbor.

2154.t: From Biblical Hebrew יוֹחָנָן (yōḥɔnɔn), the masculine form of יוֹחָנָה (yōḥānā), whence also Ἰωάννα (Ĭōắnnā).

2130.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰn̥gʰ-ú-s, zero-grade u-stem of *dʰengʰ- (“to go quickly”), based on the comparison with Lithuanian déngti (“to run, hurry”) (see there for more potential cognates), though Fraenkel has disputed the connection.

2143.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hā́ls, from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l (“salt”). Cognates include Sanskrit सलिल (salila), Old Armenian աղ (ał), Latin sāl, and Old English sealt (English salt).

2158.t: Genitive singular of ὁμός (homós, “same”), used adverbially.

2168.t: From Old Persian 𐎱𐎠𐎼𐎿 (p-a-r-s /⁠Pārsa⁠/) + -ις (-ĭs, feminine suffix).

2133.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰugā́, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰugéh₂. Equivalent to φεύγω (pheúgō, “flee”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

2108.t: Already in Late Mycenaean Greek (Ta-716 from Pylos), attested in the dual 𐀥𐀯𐀟𐀁 (qi-si-pe-e, “two swords”) (mostly ideographically as 𐃉).

2179.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ (“two”), with δύο (dŭ́o) coming from the indeclinable variant *d(u)wó.

2189.t: From μνάομαι (mnáomai, “to be mindful of, remember”) + -μη (-mē).

2172.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *mergʰ- (“to moisten, wet”) via a metathesized schwebeablaut form of *mregʰ- or zero-grade form *mr̥gʰ-; cognates include Latvian merguot (“to rain slowly”), merga (“soft rain”).

2173.t: Seemingly imitative of croaking, with original form something like *βρατ-αχ- (*brat-akh-), but this imitation was probably not formed in Greek, but borrowed from Pre-Greek or Semitic; compare Hebrew צְפַרְדֵּעַ (ṣəp̄ardḗaʿ), Arabic ضَفْدَع (ḍafdaʕ),…

2178.t: Morphologically from δια- (dia-) + στῆναι (stênai) + -μα (-ma), from ἵστημι (hístēmi).

2126.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tségʷomai, from Proto-Indo-European *tyegʷ- (“avoid, yield to”).

2134.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰúyō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuHyéti, from *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

2152.t: * Masculine from Proto-Hellenic *hwādús, from Proto-Indo-European *swéh₂dus. * Feminine from Proto-Hellenic *hwādéyya, from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₂déwih₂: see -ια (-ia). Both forms are regardless from *sweh₂d- (“to be sweet”).

2136.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰolā́, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰolh₃-éh₂, from *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”).

2156.t: From Proto-Hellenic *opʰél͏̌l͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰélyeti, from *h₃bʰel- (whence ὄφελος (óphelos, “benefit”)).

2197.t: Derived from Proto-Indo-European *p(y)eh₂w- (“to hit, strike”). Cognates include Latin paviō.

2100.t: For μετήορος (metḗoros), from μετά (metá, “beyond”) + *ἀορος (*aoros), an o-grade noun from ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift up, raise”).

2171.t: From βόσκω (bóskō, “to feed, tend”) + -άνη (-ắnē, instrument noun suffix).

2191.t: A Kulturwort which spread to various other languages, of disputed origin: * Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *smer- (“to anoint, smear”), along with σμύρις (smúris, “emery”), and connected with Proto-Indo-European *smérus (“grease”) (whence…

2150.t: From ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bring, bear, carry”).

2132.t: From τιτρώσκω (titrṓskō, “to wound”) + -μα (-mă, suffix forming neuter nouns).

2124.t: Abstract noun from σύμμαχος (súmmakhos, “fighting together”) + -ία (-íā, abstract noun suffix).

2188.t: From μνήμη (mnḗmē, “memory”) + -εῖον (-eîon), from μνάομαι (mnắomai, “I am mindful of”) + -μη (-mē).

2198.t: From πληρόω (plēróō, “to fill”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

2121.t: Disputedly cognate with Middle Irish serb (“theft”), pointing to Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“to rob”), but this is uncertain.

2196.t: From παρακαλέω (părăkăléō, “to summon, encourage”) (from παρά (părắ, “near”) + καλέω (kăléō, “to call”)) + -σις (-sĭs).

2139.t: The first element is ἄκρος (ắkros, “topmost; outermost”). The second element is uncertain; it was traditionally thought to be βύω (bŭ́ō, “to stuff; to plug”), but this is almost certainly incorrect.

2160.t: Contraction of ὑπερώϊος (hŭperṓĭ̈os), from ὑπέρ (hŭpér, “above; over”).

2180.t: From Proto-Indo-European *denḱ- (“to bite”). Cognate with Sanskrit दशति (daśati, “to bite”), Old English ġetingan (“to press upon”), and Albanian darë.

2194.t: There are no obvious cognates. If connected with Latin natis (“rump”), it can be either assumed a derivation from an old Proto-Indo-European root noun *n(e)h₃t- or a root *nh₂t-, which became thematicized in Greek.

2164.t: From ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”) + -η (-ē), possibly inherited from Proto-Hellenic *hrowā́, from Proto-Indo-European *srowéh₂, from the root *srew- (“to flow, stream”).

2127.t: A Semitic loanword, found as Aramaic סָסָא / ܣܳܣܳܐ (sāsā, “moth”), Hebrew סָס (sās, “moth”), Akkadian 𒌨𒈨 (sāsum, “moth”), Arabic سُوس (sūs, “moth-worm”).

2151.t: From ἔδω (édō, “to eat”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

2138.t: The formation is similar to κάμαξ (kắmăx, “vine pole; prop”) and πίναξ (pĭ́năx, “board; plank”), and the traditional connection with Lithuanian žer̃ti (“to scrape”) does not explain the Greek formation.

2163.t: From ῥάπτω (rhắptō, “to sew together, stitch”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

2153.t: Beekes suggests an equivalence with Latin vallus (“stake; pole”) on the basis of the Aeolic variant ϝάλλος (wắllos), in which case from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn”).

2195.t: From οἶκος (oîkos, “house, home, estate”) + νόμος (nómos, “law, rule, authority”), equivalent to οἶκος (oîkos) + νέμω (némō) + -ος (-os).

2102.t: Denominative in -ύνω (-ū́nō), like παλύνω (pălū́nō, “to bestrew; to besprinkle”) and φορύνω (phorū́nō, “to be mingled”), from an unattested base form.

2187.t: By surface analysis, λούω (loúō, “to wash, bathe”) + -τήρ (-tḗr). Compare λουτρόν (loutrón, “bathing-place”).

2137.t: From χρίω (khríō, “to rub, smear, anoint”) + -σις (-sis), forming an action noun.
